specName: A living spec is read one requirement at a time
last_action: living specs loaded (capture-runtime, spec-viewer, companion-commands, viewer-ui, specs)

FR-001.title: A requirement MAY carry one marker naming the files it describes, ignored by every existing reader.

FR-002.title: A requirement with no marker is treated as describing every file its capability claims.

FR-003.title: A marked spec contributes its purpose, matching requirements, and unmarked requirements — nothing else.

FR-004.title: A spec with no markers loads whole, unchanged from today.

FR-005.title: A run records which requirements it loaded, without changing the existing capability record shape.

FR-006.title: Adoption writes a marker on each requirement it produces.

FR-007.title: A sync writes or widens the marker of each requirement it updates.

FR-008.title: Requirement parsing ignores fenced code blocks and both implementations count the same headings.

FR-009.title: A living spec renders an outline of its requirement headings in document order.

FR-010.title: An outline row shows known coverage, and shows unknown coverage as unknown rather than none.

FR-011.title: An outline row indicates how many files its marker names, and nothing where there is no marker.

FR-012.title: Activating an outline row moves the view to that requirement, by pointer and keyboard.

FR-013.title: A feature spec does not render the outline.

FR-014.title: Fold, drift, sync, coverage and adoption behave identically with or without markers.

FR-015.title: The on-disk format, the registry and its ordering do not otherwise change.

intent: Make the requirement, not the file, the unit a living spec is loaded and navigated by, so a spec of any size costs a run only the requirements that matter.
expectations: Validation, fold-back refusal, editor diagnostics and the retire guard (Wave 2)
Splitting the four large specs — measured after this lands
context: living spec: capture-runtime, spec-viewer, companion-commands, viewer-ui, specs
area: livingSpecsModel.ts requirementIds, resolve-spec-paths.py, livingComponents.ts requirement cards
constraint: on-disk format additive only; registry and glob ordering unchanged; both parsers must count the same headings
approach: A requirement gains an optional HTML-comment marker naming the files it describes; adoption and sync write it as a by-product. The load step then contributes a capability's purpose, the requirements whose marker matches a changed file, and every unmarked requirement, instead of the whole spec. The viewer derives a requirement outline from the pass that already builds requirement cards.

decisions.decision: The marker is an HTML comment on the line under the requirement heading
decisions.why: The hard constraint is that no existing reader changes behaviour; an HTML comment is invisible to every markdown renderer and matches the <!-- capability: … --> convention fold-back already uses
decisions.rejected: Per-requirement frontmatter (impossible — document-level), a sidecar map (drifts on rename), an attribute on the heading (changes the join key fold-back and coverage match on)

decisions.decision: Marker globs reuse each side existing registry matcher
decisions.why: Two glob dialects in one feature is a bug generator, and a marker is the same kind of statement as a capability match list
decisions.rejected: A stricter prefix-only form, or a new matcher tuned for markers — both would drift from registry semantics

decisions.decision: Requirement slicing is implemented twice and pinned by one shared fixture set
decisions.why: Forced — the viewer has no Python and the command bodies have no TypeScript; the risk is divergence not duplication, and core.spec.md already prescribes pinning two runtimes against shared cases
decisions.rejected: Parse only in Python and round-trip from the viewer (slower, new failure mode at paint time); parse only in TS and shell out (command bodies must work with no extension installed)

decisions.decision: An unmarked requirement is contributed by every load
decisions.why: This is the safety property: a marker can only narrow, so a missing or too-narrow marker costs a run an extra requirement rather than starving it of one
decisions.rejected: Unmarked means loaded only when nothing else matched — makes one requirement load depend on another marker

decisions.decision: The outline is derived in the requirement-card pass
decisions.why: The spec forbids a second parse, and that pass already walks every heading and already keys coverage by the same verbatim text, so a row and its card cannot disagree
decisions.rejected: A separate outline component re-parsing the markdown — the exact mechanism by which the two could diverge

plan.summary: Additive marker + selective load + an outline derived from the existing card pass; two parsers pinned by shared fixtures.
plan.key_finding: The manifest of what to load is already computable — the resolver knows the changed files and the renderer already walks every heading; the feature is mostly wiring what exists, plus one genuinely duplicated parser that has to be pinned.

tasks.summary: 26 tasks across 6 phases: a Foundational phase that pins the two parsers against shared fixtures blocks all three stories; markers are written before the load narrows on them, and the outline lands last.
